subject.title: Document/support Android via Termux+proot: sdcardfs hazards (no symlink/exec, stale st_size) can corrupt git workflows

question: Should OpenClaw document Termux/proot as an unsupported-but-usable Android Gateway host with a shared-storage warning, or retain the current supported-host boundary and route this guidance to community/Termux documentation?
rationale: The proposed wording changes the project’s practical support promise: current Android documentation says the app is a companion node and that Android does not host the Gateway, while the requested note would tell users how to run one there.

options.title: Add an unsupported-host caution
options.body: Recommended: document Termux/proot as community-tested but unsupported, require private `$HOME` storage for dependencies and workspaces, and avoid a Doctor check for now.

options.title: Adopt a supported Android host path
options.body: Expand the Android support contract, then define tested Termux/proot versions, lifecycle limitations, and a maintained diagnostic path before publishing setup instructions.

options.title: Keep core docs to supported hosts
options.body: Retain the current platform boundary and point Termux users to community-maintained setup guidance without adding an OpenClaw support promise.

recommendation.title: Add an unsupported-host caution
recommendation.body: Recommended: document Termux/proot as community-tested but unsupported, require private `$HOME` storage for dependencies and workspaces, and avoid a Doctor check for now.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent Termux compatibility work was included in a public release associated with this account, and the decision changes the documented Android hosting model.
